resolutions.title: A duplicated `## Decisions` or `## Mechanism` heading silently replaces the earlier section, dropping a live rule and reporting a false orphan
resolutions.action: collectSections (explore-counter.ts) now MERGES a same-named `##` section into the earlier one in file order (lines and entries appended) and records every heading line in Section.headings; parseExploreRules surfaces one note per extra `## Decisions` / `## Mechanism` heading. First-key-wins therefore holds across the whole file: the external half's reproduction (second Mechanism section) now yields D-x-1 no-closure + D-x-9 orphan + D-x-1 duplicate, and the fresh half's (second Decisions section) keeps D-x-1. Fixtures for both in explore-rules.test.ts and the merge in explore-counter.test.ts.

resolutions.title: `TABLE_CELL_ROW` rejects GFM-valid member rows, so trailing whitespace flips an accounted rule into the verb-changing Unaccounted cell
resolutions.action: TABLE_CELL_ROW and TABLE_HEADER regexes replaced by GFM row predicates in explore-grammar.ts: splitTableRow (trim; one optional leading and trailing pipe; split on unescaped `|`; cells trimmed), isMemberRow (exactly two non-empty cells), isTableHeader (cells `member`, `covered by`); a row is detected by TABLE_ROW_START (up to three spaces then a pipe, per GFM). `|a|b|`, padded cells, a trailing space and an escaped pipe all accept; three cells and an empty cell stay MALFORMED. The surface test imports the predicates.

resolutions.title: The bare tier's `also:` line still renders a concluded exploration as `(exploring)`
resolutions.action: status.ts also: line renders an explore entry by its engine position (`exploring` / `concluded`, falling back to `exploring` only when position is absent) instead of the literal; CLI test demotes a concluded explore below a newer workstream and asserts `(concluded)`.

resolutions.title: `re_entry` is specified as present "iff exactly one" live carrier and, in the same sentence, as the first of two

resolutions.title: `readStatus` is byte-anchored: a UTF-8 BOM or trailing whitespace on the header line silently reads `exploring`
resolutions.action: readStatus strips a leading UTF-8 BOM and trimEnd()s the first non-blank line BEFORE the owned production matches (the production is unchanged). No near-miss note: the spec says a neither-token first line is never MALFORMED, and prose after the concluded token still reads exploring by the production. Fixtures for BOM, trailing whitespace and the trailing-prose case.

resolutions.title: A `D-`-prefixed heading that fails the ID grammar is reported as an orphan keyed by its whole heading text
resolutions.action: readMechanism keys a `D-` heading that fails the entry grammar by its ID-shaped prefix (DECISION_ID_PREFIX, exported from the grammar module) when one exists, so `### D-x-1: a rule` joins D-x-1 as malformed-entry naming the heading line — one report, a real ID; a heading with no ID-shaped prefix (e.g. uppercase) stays an orphan keyed by the raw token before the first ` — `. Fixture for both.

resolutions.title: The opener prefix requires `: ` with a trailing space, so a title wrapped immediately after the colon loses its ID and orphans its entry
resolutions.action: DECISION_OPENER_PREFIX terminator is now `:(?: |$)`; the owner sentence in this change's orbit-conventions delta gained the clarification (`followed by a space or the line end … the title itself may begin on the next line`). Fixture: a title wrapped immediately after the colon keeps its ID; a colon glued to the title (`D-x-1:title`) is still not the prefix.
